debug.title: Debug
debug.developerModeHint: Turning it off hides Debug from the settings and sets the log level back to the default
debug.logLevelDebugHint: Records more detail, and the log files grow faster
debug.diagnosticsHint: A summary of this app's version, plugins and settings, plus the log files. Account names are left out.
debug.exportReminderBody: The file holds this app's version, plugins, settings and recent log records. Cookies, tokens and signed URLs are masked and account names are left out, but check the content once more before you send it to anyone.
debug.logClearBody: This deletes this run's records and the log files on this device. It can't be undone.
debug.netEmptyHint: Requests the app sends during this run appear here.
debug.hcHint: Runs each installed, enabled plugin's check cases over the real network (cases that need a login use the stored credentials). One plugin at a time.
debug.hcNotLoaded: Cannot check: the plugin is not loaded (see the log)
debug.pdHint: Each plugin directory in the folder (one .js, checks.json, fixtures/) is loaded as "in development" and replaces the installed plugin with the same id; press Reload after editing. The mode only decides how a case runs, each in its own isolated environment (empty storage and credentials); everywhere else in the app a plugin in development always uses the real network.
debug.pdFolderEmpty: The folder has no plugin directory (a folder with one .js file)
debug.pdDuplicateId: {first} and {second} have the same plugin id "{id}"; only {first} is loaded
debug.pdIdChanged: The plugin id changed to "{id}"; rescan the folder
debug.pdRecordWarning: Recording uses the real network; the files of that capability in fixtures/ are overwritten only when the result matches checks.json (hand-edited ones are skipped). Undo a bad recording with git checkout in the plugin folder.
debug.pdSkippedLogin: Skipped: needs a login, not logged in
debug.pdSkippedEdited: Skipped: the fixtures were edited by hand
debug.pbEmptyHint: Play something or queue a track and the backend, stream and queue show up here.
debug.pbTemporary: Temporary play (the current index is where the queue resumes)
debug.pbLive: Listening to a live room (returns to the queue when stopped)
debug.dbViolation: {table} rowid {rowId} has no matching row in {parent}
debug.resetBody: Clears the database (settings, playlists, queue and play history), every source's login credentials, the login web view data and the cache, then restarts the app. Log files, backups and downloaded files are left alone.
debug.resetBackupNote: The database is backed up to the backups folder in the data directory first; if the backup fails nothing is cleared. Credentials are not in the backup, so you sign in again after restoring.
debug.resetBackupFailed: Could not back up the database, nothing was cleared: {message}
debug.resetConfirmBody: The database was backed up to {path}. "Clear and restart" clears the database, credentials, login web view data and cache, and cannot be undone except through that backup.
debug.resetRestartsItself: The app restarts by itself afterwards.
debug.resetRestartsManually: The app closes afterwards; open it again yourself.
debug.resetUnderstand: I understand this clears all data
debug.dbBackUpFailed: Could not back up the database: {message}
debug.dbRestoreEmpty: There are no backups. Press "Back up now"; resetting data also creates one.
debug.dbRestoreListFailed: Could not read the backup list: {message}
debug.dbCheckProblemsActions: You can restore from a backup or reset the data.

backup.intro: A backup holds your playlists, settings, installed plugins and more. It does not include sign-ins, cookies, the cache or downloaded files. Restoring replaces the current data and keeps the sign-ins on this device.
backup.rejectedNewer: This backup comes from a newer version of FMP. Update FMP first.
backup.rejectedNotFmp: This is not an FMP backup.
backup.restoreBody: The current data is replaced; a backup of it is made first. The sign-ins on this device are kept.
backup.restartsItself: The app restarts by itself afterwards.
backup.restartsManually: The app closes afterwards; open it again yourself.
backup.indexesHeading: Custom plugin indexes this backup adds
backup.unusableHeading: These plugins cannot be used in this version and will not be restored
backup.legacyChooseTitle: Where do you want to import the old data from?
backup.legacyFromDatabaseMissing: Old database (not found on this device)
backup.legacyHint: Data from the old FMP is on this device and has not been imported yet.
backup.legacyConfirmBody: This replaces the current playlists, tracks, play history, queue and radio stations, and the settings the old version has. The installed plugins, their settings and the sign-ins on this device are kept. A backup is made first.
backup.legacyBackupNoQueue: An old backup file has no queue, so the queue will be empty afterwards.
backup.legacyRejectedNotBackup: This is not a backup file of the old FMP.
backup.legacyRejectedNewer: This backup comes from a newer version of FMP and cannot be imported.
backup.legacyRejectedEmpty: This backup has nothing to import.

accounts.cookieStep1: Sign in to the website in a browser on your computer.
accounts.cookieStep2: Press F12 to open the developer tools, reload the page in the Network tab and pick a request to that website.
accounts.cookieStep3: Find "Cookie" in the request headers, copy the whole value and paste it above.
accounts.cookieFile: You can also paste a cookies.txt file (Netscape format) exported by a browser extension.
accounts.cookieWarning: Cookies are your sign-in. Don't share them. FMP keeps them only on this device.
accounts.cookieEmpty: No cookies found. Paste name=value pairs or the contents of a cookies.txt file.
accounts.cookieRejected: {name} didn't accept these cookies. Copy them again from a page where you're signed in.
